name: Rosewood Matakauri Lodge
positioning: Lakeside lodge just outside Queenstown's town center, facing Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables; officially named Rosewood Matakauri
best_for: Travelers who want lake and mountain views with helicopter, heli-ski and wine outings arranged for them
Groups or families wanting a villa with a fully equipped kitchen

facts.text: The lodge is just outside Queenstown's town center, with a view of Lake Wakatipu.
It faces The Remarkables, the mountain range across the lake.
The resort has floor-to-ceiling windows that frame the lake view from bed.
The Dining Room serves a la carte breakfast and dinner menus that celebrate local seasonal produce.
The Remarkables Terrace offers alfresco dining overlooking native gardens, with views of Lake Wakatipu and the surrounding mountains.
Private dining ranges from fireside dinners in the Library to gatherings in the Main Dining Room.
The Grand Lake View Suite has a mountain view, an open fireplace and a private balcony.
The Lake View Two Bedroom Villa has two ensuite bedrooms and a living area that overlooks the mountains.
The Matakauri Four Bedroom Villa has an open fireplace, a fully equipped kitchen with an infinity-edge jacuzzi, and a sheltered courtyard.
Heli-skiing and heli-boarding adventures in Queenstown's backcountry can be arranged.
The concierge can organize private wine tastings in the Otago wine country and helicopter rides to the peaks across the lake.
Guests can take a gourmet picnic hamper of local food and wine out into the landscape.

highlights.text: Double Rock Farm in the Kawarau Gorge grows organic berries, quince, hazelnuts and mulberries exclusively for the lodge's kitchen.
Bees at the lodge produce honey that is used in its cuisine.
A garden of rare produce, just steps away, inspires the lodge's dining.
The lodge offers scenic helicopter trips to Milford Sound.
Stargazing under New Zealand's dark sky is one of the lodge's experiences.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler finds the restaurant a little formal and suggests eating in town if you do not want a three-course meal every night.
Conde Nast Traveler notes the lodge could benefit from more amenities.

sources.title: Rosewood Matakauri review - Conde Nast Traveler
